title: Banana Oat Porridge
author: everyday
description: Creamy rolled oats simmered in milk, topped with banana and cinnamon. A simple warm breakfast with a naturally sweet finish.
steps: Combine the oats, milk and salt in a saucepan. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Reduce the heat and cook for 8–10 minutes, stirring often, until the oats are tender and creamy. Add a splash of water if needed.
Divide between two bowls. Slice the bananas, arrange them on top and sprinkle with cinnamon.

title: Avocado Egg Toast
author: everyday
description: Crisp sourdough topped with lemony mashed avocado and poached eggs. Make the eggs firm or soft to suit your preference.
steps: Toast the sourdough until golden. Mash the avocado with the lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Bring a saucepan of water to a gentle simmer. Crack each egg into a small cup and slide into the water. Poach for 3–5 minutes, or longer for a firm yolk.
Spread the avocado over the toast. Lift out the eggs with a slotted spoon, drain well and place on top. Serve immediately.

title: Greek Chickpea Salad
author: everyday
description: Chickpeas, crunchy cucumber, tomatoes and feta tossed in a lemon and olive oil dressing. An easy salad that keeps well for lunch.
steps: Drain and rinse the chickpeas. Dice the cucumber and tomatoes, thinly slice the onion and crumble the feta.
Whisk the olive oil with the lemon juice and oregano in a large bowl.
Add the chickpeas, vegetables, olives and feta. Toss gently and let stand for 10 minutes before serving. Refrigerate leftovers promptly.

title: Creamy Broccoli Soup
author: everyday
description: A smooth green soup made with broccoli, potato and a little cream. Blend until silky and adjust the thickness with stock.
steps: Chop the onion and garlic. Peel and dice the potato; cut the broccoli into small florets and dice the tender stalk.
Heat the oil in a saucepan. Soften the onion for 5 minutes, add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds.
Add the potato and stock. Simmer for 10 minutes, then add the broccoli and cook for 6–8 minutes until tender.
Blend carefully until smooth, keeping the blender lid vented if blending hot soup. Stir in the cream and salt, warm through and serve.

title: Turkey Vegetable Stir-Fry
author: everyday
description: Turkey strips and colourful vegetables in a quick soy, ginger and garlic sauce. Serve as it is or with rice prepared separately.
steps: Slice the turkey into thin strips. Cut the broccoli small, slice the pepper and carrot, and mince the garlic and ginger.
Mix the soy sauce, cornstarch and 80 ml water. Heat half the oil in a large pan and cook the turkey for 5–7 minutes until cooked through; transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and vegetables. Stir-fry for 4–5 minutes, adding a splash of water to help the broccoli soften.
Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds. Return the turkey, pour in the sauce and simmer for 2 minutes until thickened. Check the turkey is fully cooked before serving.

title: Garlic Butter White Beans
author: everyday
description: Tender white beans warmed in a glossy garlic butter sauce with lemon and parsley. A comforting one-pan meal or side dish.
steps: Drain and rinse the beans. Thinly slice the garlic and chop the parsley.
Melt the butter over medium-low heat. Cook the garlic for 1 minute without browning.
Add the beans and stock. Simmer gently for 8–10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce lightly coats the beans.
Stir in the lemon juice, parsley and pepper. Taste and serve warm.

title: Tuna Sweetcorn Wraps
author: everyday
description: Soft wraps filled with tuna, sweetcorn, crisp lettuce and a yogurt dressing. A convenient lunch assembled in minutes.
steps: Drain the tuna and sweetcorn thoroughly. Wash and dry the lettuce.
Mix the tuna, sweetcorn, yogurt, lemon juice and pepper in a bowl.
Lay lettuce down the centre of each tortilla, add the filling, fold in the sides and roll tightly. Cut in half and serve, or refrigerate until needed.

title: Spinach Ricotta Pasta
author: everyday
description: Penne coated in a creamy ricotta sauce with wilted spinach and Parmesan. Pasta cooking water brings the sauce together without extra cream.
steps: Cook the pasta in salted boiling water according to the packet. Reserve 200 ml cooking water before draining.
Heat the oil in a large pan, add the minced garlic and cook for 30 seconds. Add the spinach and stir until wilted.
Lower the heat. Stir in the ricotta, grated Parmesan, lemon juice and 100 ml reserved water.
Add the pasta and toss gently. Add more cooking water a little at a time until the sauce coats the penne. Serve straight away.

title: Roasted Vegetable Couscous
author: everyday
description: Fluffy couscous with roasted courgette, pepper, carrot and onion. Lemon and olive oil keep the finished dish bright and simple.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Cut the vegetables into evenly sized bite-sized pieces.
Toss the vegetables with the oil and salt on a roasting tray. Roast for 25 minutes, turning halfway, until tender and lightly browned.
Put the couscous in a heatproof bowl. Pour over the boiling stock, cover and leave for 5 minutes; fluff with a fork.
Fold in the roasted vegetables and lemon juice. Serve warm or cool and refrigerate promptly.

title: Yogurt Berry Parfait
author: everyday
description: Layers of Greek yogurt, fresh berries and oat granola served in glasses. Add the granola shortly before eating to keep it crisp.
steps: Wash the berries and dry gently. Hull and slice the strawberries.
Stir the honey into the yogurt. Spoon a little yogurt into each of two glasses, followed by berries and granola.
Repeat the layers and finish with a few berries. Serve immediately, or keep yogurt and fruit chilled and add the granola just before serving.

title: Potato Leek Soup
author: weekend
description: A mellow soup of potatoes and leeks, finished with a splash of cream. Wash the leeks carefully to remove grit between the layers.
steps: Trim and slice the leeks, then rinse thoroughly in a bowl of water and drain. Peel and dice the potatoes.
Melt the butter in a saucepan. Soften the leeks over medium-low heat for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Add the potatoes and stock. Bring to a simmer and cook for 15–20 minutes until the potatoes are tender.
Blend carefully until smooth, or leave a few pieces for texture. Stir in the cream, salt and pepper and warm through before serving.

title: Beef Mushroom Stew
author: weekend
description: Slow-simmered beef with mushrooms and carrots in a rich stock-based gravy. Give the beef time to become tender before serving.
steps: Cut the beef into 3 cm cubes. Slice the onion, carrots and mushrooms, and mince the garlic.
Heat the oil in a heavy casserole. Brown the beef in batches and set aside. Soften the onion and carrots for 5 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 5 minutes. Stir in the garlic, tomato paste and flour and cook for 1 minute.
Return the beef and add the stock, thyme and salt. Bring to a gentle simmer, cover and cook for 90–110 minutes until the beef is tender, stirring occasionally.
Uncover for the final 10 minutes to reduce the gravy. Add water if it becomes too thick and serve hot.

title: Lemon Herb Roast Chicken
author: weekend
description: A whole chicken roasted with lemon, rosemary and thyme. Rest before carving and use a thermometer to check the thickest parts are cooked.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C. Pat the chicken dry with kitchen paper; do not rinse it. Put it in a roasting dish.
Rub with oil, salt and pepper. Cut the lemon in half and place it in the cavity with the garlic and herbs.
Roast for approximately 80–90 minutes. Check with a food thermometer that the thickest parts of the breast and thigh reach 74°C, avoiding bone; extend cooking if needed.
Rest for 15 minutes before carving. Spoon over the roasting juices and serve.

title: Stuffed Bell Peppers
author: weekend
description: Bell pepper halves filled with beef, rice and tomato, baked with cheddar. Cook the rice separately before mixing it into the filling.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C. Cook the rice according to the packet. Halve the peppers lengthways and remove the seeds.
Heat the oil in a pan and soften the chopped onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic and beef and cook for 8–10 minutes, breaking up the beef, until cooked through.
Add the tomatoes, oregano and salt. Simmer for 8 minutes and stir in the cooked rice.
Arrange the peppers in a baking dish, fill with the mixture and top with grated cheddar. Add 100 ml water to the bottom of the dish.
Cover with foil and bake for 20 minutes. Remove the foil and bake for 10–15 minutes more until the peppers are tender and the cheese is golden.

title: Vegetable Lasagne
author: weekend
description: Layers of tomato vegetables, pasta and a simple white sauce, topped with golden cheese. Let the lasagne rest to make slicing easier.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C. Dice the onion and courgettes and slice the mushrooms. Heat the oil and soften the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the courgettes and mushrooms and cook for 8 minutes. Add minced garlic, tomatoes and half the salt. Simmer for 15 minutes, then stir in the spinach until wilted.
For the white sauce, melt the butter in a separate saucepan. Stir in the flour for 1 minute. Gradually whisk in the milk and simmer, stirring, until thickened; add the remaining salt.

Layer the vegetable sauce, lasagne sheets and white sauce in a baking dish. Repeat, finishing with white sauce and shredded mozzarella. Follow the pasta packet instructions if pre-cooking is required.
Bake for 35–40 minutes until bubbling and the pasta is tender. Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.

title: Apple Cinnamon French Toast
author: weekend
description: Golden egg-dipped bread served with soft cinnamon apples and maple syrup. Slightly stale bread holds its shape well in the egg mixture.
steps: Core and slice the apples. Melt half the butter in a pan and cook the apples with half the cinnamon for 6–8 minutes until softened.
Whisk the eggs, milk and remaining cinnamon in a shallow dish. Dip the bread briefly on both sides without soaking it until it falls apart.
Melt the remaining butter in a frying pan. Cook the bread for 3–4 minutes per side until golden and the egg mixture is cooked through.
Serve topped with the warm apples and maple syrup.

title: Baked Cod with Tomatoes
author: weekend
description: Cod fillets baked over cherry tomatoes with garlic and olive oil. The tomatoes release their juices to make a light sauce.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Halve the tomatoes and put them in a baking dish with thinly sliced garlic, half the oil and half the salt.
Roast the tomatoes for 10 minutes. Pat the cod dry and arrange on top. Drizzle with the remaining oil, lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Bake for 12–15 minutes, depending on thickness, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily; check the centre reaches 63°C.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley and spoon the tomato juices over the fish to serve.

title: Sweet Potato Black Bean Chilli
author: weekend
description: A thick vegetarian chilli with sweet potato, black beans and peppers. Adjust the chilli powder to your preferred level of heat.
steps: Peel the sweet potatoes and cut into 2 cm cubes. Chop the onion and pepper, mince the garlic and drain the beans.
Heat the oil in a saucepan. Soften the onion and pepper for 6 minutes. Add the garlic, cumin and chilli powder and stir for 30 seconds.
Add the sweet potato, tomatoes, stock and salt. Simmer, partly covered, for 20–25 minutes until the sweet potato is tender.
Stir in the beans and simmer for 5–8 minutes more. Add water if needed and adjust the seasoning before serving.

title: Strawberry Cheesecake Cups
author: weekend
description: No-bake cheesecake cream layered with biscuit crumbs and strawberries. Chill for at least two hours before serving; chilling time is additional to preparation time.
steps: Crush the biscuits into crumbs and mix with the melted butter. Divide among four small glasses and press lightly.
Beat the cream cheese, yogurt, icing sugar and vanilla until smooth. Spoon over the biscuit bases.
Wash, hull and slice the strawberries and arrange on top.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours before serving. Keep chilled until ready to eat.

title: Pear Walnut Crumble
author: weekend
description: Tender baked pears under a crisp oat and walnut topping. Serve warm after a short rest so the fruit juices settle.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C. Core the pears and cut into bite-sized pieces. Toss with lemon juice and cinnamon in a baking dish.
Rub the cold butter into the flour until crumbly. Stir in the oats, chopped walnuts and sugar.
Scatter the topping evenly over the pears without pressing down. Bake for 30–35 minutes until golden and the fruit is tender.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving warm.
